Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.
I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both required control skills before proposing or editing the single candidate.

I’m using `fish-control-primitives` because the requested transfer protocol requires it, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because this workspace requires both moving-window views to be inspected before policy changes. I’ll use the shelf only for a transferable feedback invariant, not scalar gain tuning.

`rg` is not installed in this workspace, so I’m using a read-only file inventory instead. The sampled scores are all captures; I’m checking their timing, route, actuation, and wake details to identify the strongest finite run and the most informative regression rather than treating score alone as the ranking.

The evidence isolates a clean positive mechanism: the evaluated one-sided speed-envelope projection preserved capture and the same target-crossing wake, improved arrival and score, cut mean requested acceleration, and reduced outward-at-limit commands without changing any carrier gain. I’m now consulting the shelf references to express only that actuator-feasibility invariant in the required body-frame/two-joint contract.

The shelf reinforces preserving the traveling-wave carrier and keeping bounded feedback corrections distinct from propulsion. I’m recording the visual diagnosis and the single hypothesis now, before touching the candidate: promote the completed narrow, one-sided speed-feasibility projection—no gain changes and no added route logic.

The candidate now contains only the evaluated final-one-percent projection. I’m distilling the reusable result into guidance with its important boundary: it reduced infeasible outward requests and loads, but did not reduce near-speed residence, so later workers should not reinterpret it as generic carrier derating.

The candidate exactly matches the completed best sampled implementation, and both provenance files are updated. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner now; if it reports any contract failure, I’ll repair and rerun it.
The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this account, so the invocation could not start. I’m following the same TOML instructions directly and running its three non-CFD checks separately.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract check is blocked only because `julia` is absent from the default PATH (the login profile also emitted unrelated SSH setup noise), so I’m locating the workspace’s Julia runtime and will rerun the same check without the login profile.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl) — evaluated final-1% one-sided joint-speed feasibility guard.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md) — visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md) — reusable evidence-backed actuator-feasibility lesson.

All three prescribed non-CFD checks passed: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract/schema, and workspace boundary. Formal CFD was not run.
